newsitem.title: USA: Ralston withdraws in adultery controversy.
newsitem.headline: Ralston withdraws in adultery controversy.

text.p: Air Force Gen. Joseph Ralston on Monday withdrew from consideration to become chairman of the U.S. military Joint Chiefs of Staff in an uproar over an adulterous affair he had 13 years ago.
But Defense Secretary Willian Cohen announced that he had asked Ralston, 53, to remain as vice chairman of the joint chiefs and that Ralston had agreed.
"This is solely my decision and I make it with a sense of regret," Ralston said in a statement.

"My regret is that the public discussion surrounding my potential nomination blurred the facts in a number of recent cases and gave the appearance of a double-standard regarding military justice," he said.

Ralston admitted last week that he had an adulterous relationship while separated from his first wife more than a decade ago. That came just after the Air Force forced its first woman bomber pilot to resign to avoid a court martial on adultery and other charges, sparking charges in Congress of uneven application of military justice.
Members of Congress warned after the controversy broke that the Senate might reject Ralston if he were to be nominated by President Bill Clinton for the joint chiefs' leadership.
